title: Address cumulative rounding and export idempotency in multi-rate proration pipeline
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: Several customers have reported small but systematic invoice mismatches between the amounts billed in Stripe and the amounts posted to NetSuite after scheduled billing runs. Finance observed cumulative drift for multi-rate plans (combination of per-token and tiered subscription fees) resulting in NetSuite ledger mismatches and manual reconciliation overhead. Investigation found two compounding issues: 1) per-line floating-point rounding (python floats) applied independently per charge line produced cumulative cent-level drift on invoices with many partial charges; 2) the billing export pipeline to NetSuite lacked true idempotency and export manifests, enabling rare duplicate export attempts during retries that then got partially reconciled and required correcting journal entries.
background: Redwood's billing pipeline splits usage by rate components and prorates when plan changes or mid-period events occur. The existing implementation uses decimal rounding per line and persists intermediate floats before converting to cents at export. Export jobs use a best-effort retry path without a global export manifest or idempotency token; retry duplicates can create duplicate journal attempts which finance reconciles manually. Prior tickets touched related areas (ENG-9183, ENG-4827, ENG-10534) but did not fix the rounding allocation algorithm or export-level idempotency.
root_cause: 1) Arithmetic: using decimal/floats for intermediate sums and rounding each line independently caused unbiased but cumulatively noticeable drift on invoices with many prorated rows. 2) Export resilience: export retries do not attach a deterministic idempotency key and reconciliation manifest, so partial successes + retry windows led to duplicated net entries in NetSuite exports. 3) Cutoff alignment: timezone and billing window boundary handling caused small mismatches between Stripe's captured amounts and our NetSuite mapping for certain customers spanning regions.
proposal: A multi-pronged fix: (A) Switch all billing arithmetic to integer cents (64-bit) within the billing service and implement a balanced rounding allocator that ensures invoice-level sum preservation (distribute remainder cents across highest-precision lines deterministically). (B) Add an export manifest and idempotency token: every billing run emits a signed manifest (sha256) with sequence number and per-invoice checksums; NetSuite export job must include the manifest id and will be idempotent on manifest+invoice. (C) Add strict validation in the export step: assert invoice_total_cents == sum(line_cents) and reject exports that fail; surface these rejections to finance QA dashboard. (D) Implement backfill tooling to recompute invoices for the last 90 days that exceed a delta tolerance and produce corrective credit memos or adjustments with finance approval. (E) Add observability: metrics invoice_drift_cents, export_duplicate_attempts, manifest_mismatch_rate and a Grafana dashboard and PagerDuty alert when anomalies exceed thresholds.
rollback_plan: Feature-gate the new allocator and idempotency behavior behind a billing feature flag per-tenant. Roll back by disabling the feature flag and reverting the exporter to previous behavior; sequence numbers and manifests are read-only so no data corruption occurs. For the backfill, only run after sign-off; any corrective invoices will be reversible via credit memos from finance.
testing_plan: Unit tests for balanced rounding allocator with randomized multi-rate inputs; property-based tests to prove invoice sum invariants. Integration tests in staging that run a 30-day shadow billing (dry-run) comparing legacy and new outputs and log diffs; automated end-to-end export to a sandbox NetSuite connector with idempotency validation. Load test for large invoices to validate perf and memory. Finance-run dry run producing CSVs for accounting review before full rollout.
migration_and_backfill: Create a backfill job that recomputes invoice_cents using the new allocator and flags invoices where new_amount != posted_amount. Provide an interactive finance tool to preview recommended corrective credits with rationale and CSV export for NetSuite bulk upload. Backfill run initially in read-only mode; corrective writes gated by finance sign-off and manual runbook steps.
metrics_and_alerting: Add metrics: billing.invoice_drift_cents.p95, billing.export_duplicate_count, billing.manifest_mismatch_rate; set alerts: p95_drift > 200 cents for >1% of invoices in 24h -> P1 PagerDuty, export_duplicate_count > 5/day -> notify billing-eng on Slack channel #billing-ops. Add a daily reconciliation report emailed to finance with top 20 invoices by drift.
acceptance_criteria: All billing arithmetic uses integer-cent arithmetic in billing service and allocator preserves invoice-level totals
Balanced rounding allocator implemented and covered by unit/property tests
Export pipeline emits manifest with idempotency token and NetSuite exporter is idempotent for repeated deliveries
Staging shadow run shows net drift reduction to <= 1 cent per invoice for 99.9% of cases
Backfill identifies affected invoices from last 90 days and produces finance-validated corrective actions
Grafana dashboard and PagerDuty alerts created and verified
Finance approves dry-run CSVs and signs off on corrective workflow

notes: Edge case: customers using both pre-paid credits and post-pay billing saw larger apparent drift due to rounding across payment types; include these in backfill scope.
We must coordinate with NetSuite admin to accept manifest-based idempotency: update NetSuite connector to reject duplicate manifest+invoice tuples.
Legal/finance guidance required on customer communication for corrective credit memos; prepare template email and FAQ.
Potential follow-up: audit-run to ensure VAT/withholding tax calculations unaffected by integer-switch; include tax team in validation.
This ticket intentionally avoids changing Stripe-charge-level logic; we reconcile to Stripe amounts and post adjustments to NetSuite so we must ensure Stripe rounding invariant holds.
